title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Continued)

articles.content_en:
Article 260 For the cases provided for in Article 1 of this Interpretation, if the victim has died, lost capacity for civil conduct, or is unable to file a complaint due to coercion, intimidation, or other reasons, or is a person with limited capacity for civil conduct and is unable to file a complaint in person due to old age, illness, blindness, deafness, muteness, or other reasons, and if the legal representative or close relative files a complaint or files a complaint on behalf of the victim, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.
When the legal representative or close relative of the victim files a complaint or files a complaint on behalf of the victim, they shall provide proof of their relationship with the victim and proof of the reasons why the victim cannot file a complaint in person.

Article 261 To initiate a private prosecution, a written criminal complaint shall be submitted; if a civil action is also brought incidental to the criminal proceeding, a written criminal complaint with incidental civil action shall be submitted.

Article 264 For a private prosecution case that has already been placed on file but, upon examination, lacks evidence of the crime, if the private prosecutor cannot provide supplementary evidence, the People's Court shall persuade the private prosecutor to withdraw the prosecution or make a ruling to dismiss the prosecution; if, after withdrawing the prosecution or having the prosecution dismissed, the private prosecutor presents new evidence sufficient to prove the defendant's guilt and files a private prosecution again, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 265 If a private prosecutor refuses to accept a ruling not to accept the case or a ruling to dismiss the prosecution, he or she may file an appeal.
If the People's Court of second instance ascertains that the ruling not to accept the case made by the People's Court of first instance is erroneous, it shall, while revoking the original ruling, instruct the People's Court of first instance to place the case on file and accept it; if it ascertains that the ruling to dismiss the prosecution made by the People's Court of first instance is erroneous, it shall, while revoking the original ruling, instruct the People's Court of first instance to conduct a trial.

Article 266 If a private prosecutor knows that there are other joint infringers but only initiates a private prosecution against some of them, the People's Court shall accept the case and inform the private prosecutor of the legal consequences of abandoning the complaint; if the private prosecutor abandons the complaint and later, after the judgment is pronounced, initiates a private prosecution against other joint infringers concerning the same facts, the People's Court shall not accept the case.
If only some of the joint victims file a complaint, the People's Court shall notify the other victims to participate in the proceedings and inform them of the legal consequences of not participating. If the notified person, upon receiving the notice, indicates that he or she will not participate in the proceedings or does not appear in court, he or she shall be deemed to have abandoned the complaint. After the pronouncement of the first-instance judgment, if the notified person files a private prosecution again concerning the same facts, the People's Court shall not accept the case. However, if the party separately files a civil action, this shall not be limited by this Interpretation.

Article 267 If a defendant commits two or more criminal acts, some of which are public prosecution cases and others are private prosecution cases, the People's Court may try them together. The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to the trial of the private prosecution part.

Article 268 If a party to a private prosecution case cannot obtain evidence due to objective reasons and applies to the People's Court to obtain it, the party shall state the reasons and provide relevant clues or materials. If the People's Court deems it necessary, it shall promptly obtain the evidence.
Article 269 For a private prosecution case with clear criminal facts and sufficient evidence, a court session shall be held.

Article 270 If a private prosecution case meets the conditions for applying the summary procedure, the summary procedure may be applied.
For a private prosecution case to which the summary procedure is not applied, the relevant provisions on the ordinary procedure of first instance for public prosecution cases shall be applied mutatis mutandis.

Article 271 When trying a private prosecution case, the People's Court may, on the basis of ascertaining the facts and distinguishing right from wrong, conduct mediation based on the principles of voluntariness and lawfulness. If an agreement is reached through mediation, a written criminal mediation agreement shall be prepared, signed by the judicial officer and the court clerk, and affixed with the seal of the People's Court. The mediation agreement shall have legal effect upon receipt of the agreement by both parties. If no agreement is reached through mediation, or if a party repudiates the agreement before signing it, a judgment shall be made promptly.
Mediation shall not apply to the cases provided for in Item (3) of Article 204 of the Criminal Procedure Law.

Article 272 Before a judgment is pronounced, the parties to a private prosecution case may reach a settlement on their own, and the private prosecutor may withdraw the private prosecution.
If, upon examination, the People's Court considers that the settlement or withdrawal of the private prosecution is truly voluntary, it shall make a ruling to permit it; if it considers that it resulted from coercion, intimidation, or other factors and was not voluntary, it shall not permit it.

Article 273 If, in a private prosecution case where a ruling permits the withdrawal of the prosecution or the parties reach a settlement on their own, the defendant has been subjected to compulsory measures, the People's Court shall immediately release the defendant from such measures.

Article 274 If the private prosecutor, after being summoned twice, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, or leaves the courtroom without permission, the People's Court shall make a ruling to treat the case as withdrawn.
If some private prosecutors withdraw the prosecution or are treated as having withdrawn the prosecution by ruling, this shall not affect the continued trial of the case.

Article 275 If the defendant's whereabouts are unknown during the trial of a private prosecution case, the People's Court shall make a ruling to suspend the trial. After the defendant appears before the court, the trial shall be resumed, and compulsory measures shall be taken against the defendant according to law if necessary.

Article 276 For a private prosecution case, a judgment shall be made by referring to Article 195 of the Criminal Procedure Law and the relevant provisions of Article 241 of this Interpretation; for a case where a verdict of not guilty is pronounced according to law, the incidental civil part shall be mediated according to law or a judgment shall be made together.

Article 278 When accepting a case involving a crime committed by a unit, the People's Court shall, in addition to conducting examination in accordance with the relevant provisions of Article 180 of this Interpretation, also examine whether the bill of prosecution lists the name, domicile, contact information of the defendant unit, and the name, position, and contact information of its legal representative, principal responsible person, and the litigation representative who appears in court on behalf of the defendant unit. If the People's Procuratorate needs to supplement materials, the court shall notify the People's Procuratorate to provide them within three days.

Article 279 The litigation representative of a defendant unit shall be its legal representative or principal responsible person; if the legal representative or principal responsible person is accused as the person directly in charge of the unit crime or is unable to appear in court due to objective reasons, the defendant unit shall entrust another responsible person or employee as the litigation representative. However, this shall not apply if the person concerned is accused as another person directly responsible for the unit crime or knows the circumstances of the case and is obligated to testify.

Article 280 When trying a case involving a crime committed by a unit in a court session, the People's Court shall notify the litigation representative of the defendant unit to appear in court; if there is no litigation representative to participate in the proceedings, the court shall request the People's Procuratorate to designate one.
If the litigation representative of the defendant unit does not appear in court, the matter shall be handled according to the following circumstances:
(1) If the litigation representative is the legal representative or principal responsible person of the defendant unit and refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, he or she may be compelled to appear by a warrant; if he or she is unable to appear due to objective reasons or his or her whereabouts are unknown, the court shall request the People's Procuratorate to designate another litigation representative;
(2) If the litigation representative is another person of the defendant unit, the court shall request the People's Procuratorate to designate another litigation representative to appear in court.

Article 281 The litigation representative of a defendant unit shall enjoy the procedural rights of a defendant as provided for in the Criminal Procedure Law. During the court session, the seat of the litigation representative shall be placed on the left side in front of the judges' bench, in line with the defense counsel's seat.
Article 282 The relevant provisions of this Interpretation shall apply mutatis mutandis when a defendant unit retains a defense counsel.

Article 283 If, for a case that shall be determined as a unit crime, the People's Procuratorate only prosecutes it as a crime committed by a natural person, the People's Court shall suggest that the People's Procuratorate supplement the prosecution against the unit that committed the crime. If the People's Procuratorate still prosecutes it as a crime committed by a natural person, the People's Court shall try the case according to law, investigate the criminal liability of the person directly in charge or other persons directly responsible in the unit crime, and cite the provisions of the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law concerning the investigation of criminal liability of the person directly in charge and other persons directly responsible in a unit crime.

Article 284 If the illegal gains of the defendant unit and the proceeds derived therefrom have not been recovered or sealed up, seized, or frozen according to law, the People's Court shall decide to recover or seal up, seize, or freeze them.

Article 285 To ensure enforcement of the judgment, the People's Court may, before the judgment, seal up, seize, or freeze the property of the defendant unit, or the defendant unit may provide a guaranty.

Article 286 If, during the trial, the defendant unit is dissolved, deregistered, has its business license revoked, or is declared bankrupt, the person directly in charge and other persons directly responsible for the unit crime shall continue to be tried.

Article 287 If, during the trial, the defendant unit is merged or divided, the original unit shall be listed as the defendant unit, and the merger or division shall be noted. The fine imposed on the defendant unit shall be limited to the property and proceeds of the unit in the new unit.
Article 288 For cases involving crimes committed by a unit, matters not provided for in this Chapter shall be handled by reference to the relevant provisions of this Interpretation.

Article 289 After accepting a public prosecution case, if a Primary People's Court, upon examination, considers that the facts of the case are clear and the evidence is sufficient, when serving a copy of the bill of prosecution on the defendant, it shall inquire the defendant's opinion on the alleged criminal facts and inform him or her of the legal provisions on applying the summary procedure. If the defendant has no objection to the alleged criminal facts and agrees to the application of the summary procedure, the court may decide to apply the summary procedure and notify the People's Procuratorate and the defense counsel before the court session.
For a case where the People's Procuratorate recommends the application of the summary procedure, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph; if the conditions for applying the summary procedure are not satisfied, the People's Procuratorate shall be notified.

Article 291 For a case tried under the summary procedure, if it meets the conditions provided for in Paragraph 1 of Article 34 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the People's Court shall inform the defendant and his or her close relatives that they may apply for legal aid.

Article 292 When trying a case under the summary procedure, the People's Court shall, at least three days before the court session, notify the People's Procuratorate, the private prosecutor, the defendant, and the defense counsel of the time and place of the court session, and may also notify other participants in the proceedings.
The notification may be made in a simple manner, but it shall be recorded in the case file.
Article 293 When trying a case under the summary procedure, if the defendant has a defense counsel, the defense counsel shall be notified to appear in court.

Article 294 When trying a case under the summary procedure, the presiding judge or the sole judge shall, in court, inquire the defendant's opinion on the alleged criminal facts, inform the defendant of the legal provisions on trial under the summary procedure, and confirm whether the defendant agrees to the application of the summary procedure.

Article 296 During a sole judge trial under the summary procedure, if it is discovered that the sentence of fixed-term imprisonment that may be imposed on the defendant exceeds three years, the case shall be transferred to a collegial panel for trial.
Article 297 When trying a case under the summary procedure, the judgment shall generally be pronounced in court.

Article 299 When pronouncing a first-instance judgment or ruling, the local People's Courts at various levels shall inform the defendant, the private prosecutor, and their legal representatives that if they refuse to accept the judgment or ruling, they have the right, within the statutory period, to file an appeal in writing or orally through the current court or directly to the People's Court at the next higher level; the defendant's defense counsel or close relatives may also file an appeal with the defendant's consent; the parties to the incidental civil action and their legal representatives may file an appeal against the incidental civil part of the judgment or ruling.
Whether the defendant, private prosecutor, parties to the incidental civil action, and their legal representatives file an appeal shall be determined by their last expression of intention before the expiration of the appeal period.

Article 300 An appeal case accepted by the People's Court shall generally have the original and copies of the petition for appeal.
The content of the petition for appeal shall include: the document number of the first-instance judgment or ruling and the time when the appellant received it, the name of the People's Court of first instance, the request and reasons for the appeal, and the time when the appeal is filed. If the defendant's defense counsel or close relatives file an appeal with the defendant's consent, it shall also state their relationship with the defendant, and the defendant shall be listed as the appellant.

Article 301 An appeal or protest must be filed within the statutory period. The period for appeal or protest against a judgment is ten days; the period for appeal or protest against a ruling is five days. The period for appeal or protest shall be calculated from the day after receipt of the judgment or ruling.
The period for appeal or protest against a judgment or ruling on the incidental civil action shall be determined in accordance with the period for appeal or protest against the criminal part. If the incidental civil part is tried separately, the period for appeal shall also be determined in accordance with the period prescribed by the Criminal Procedure Law.

Article 302 If the appellant files an appeal through the People's Court of first instance, the People's Court of first instance shall examine the appeal. If the appeal complies with the provisions of the law, it shall, within three days after the expiration of the appeal period, transfer the petition for appeal together with the case file and evidence to the People's Court at the next higher level, and serve a copy of the petition for appeal on the People's Procuratorate at the same level and the opposite party.

Article 303 If the appellant files an appeal directly with the People's Court of second instance, the People's Court of second instance shall, within three days after receiving the petition for appeal, submit the petition to the People's Court of first instance. The People's Court of first instance shall examine whether the appeal complies with the provisions of the law. If it does, it shall, within three days after receiving the petition for appeal, transfer the petition together with the case file and evidence to the People's Court at the next higher level, and serve a copy of the petition for appeal on the People's Procuratorate at the same level and the opposite party.
Article 304 If the appellant requests to withdraw the appeal within the appeal period, the People's Court shall permit the withdrawal.

Article 305 If the appellant requests to withdraw the appeal after the expiration of the appeal period, the People's Court of second instance shall examine the request. Upon examination, if it considers that the facts found and the application of law in the original judgment are correct and the sentence is appropriate, it shall make a ruling to permit the withdrawal of the appeal; if it considers that the facts in the original judgment are unclear, the evidence is insufficient, or an innocent person was convicted, or a light crime was heavily punished, etc., it shall not permit the withdrawal and shall continue to try the case as an appeal case.
If a defendant sentenced to death with immediate execution files an appeal and applies for withdrawal of the appeal after the second-instance court session but before the pronouncement of the judgment, the withdrawal shall not be permitted, and the case shall continue to be tried as an appeal case.

Article 306 When a local People's Procuratorate at any level protests against a first-instance judgment or ruling of a People's Court at the same level, it shall submit the written protest through the People's Court of first instance. The People's Court of first instance shall, within three days after the expiration of the protest period, transfer the written protest together with the case file and evidence to the People's Court at the next higher level, and serve a copy of the written protest on the parties.

Article 307 If the People's Procuratorate withdraws the protest within the protest period, the People's Court of first instance shall no longer transfer the case to the People's Court at the next higher level; if the protest is withdrawn after the expiration of the protest period but before the pronouncement of the judgment by the People's Court of second instance, the People's Court of second instance may make a ruling to permit the withdrawal and notify the People's Court of first instance and the parties.

Article 308 If the appeal or protest is withdrawn before the expiration of the appeal or protest period, the first-instance judgment or ruling shall come into force on the date the appeal or protest period expires. If a request to withdraw the appeal or protest is made after the expiration of the appeal or protest period, and the People's Court of second instance makes a ruling to permit the withdrawal, the first-instance judgment or ruling shall come into force on the date the written ruling of the second instance is served on the appellant or the protesting organ.

Article 310 When adjudicating an appeal or protest case, the people's court of second instance shall conduct a comprehensive review of the facts determined and the law applied in the first instance judgment or ruling, and shall not be limited by the scope of the appeal or protest.

Article 311 In a joint crime case, where only some of the defendants have appealed, or the private prosecutor has only appealed against the judgment concerning some of the defendants, or the People's Procuratorate has only protested against the judgment concerning some of the defendants, the people's court of second instance shall review the whole case and handle it together.

Article 312 In a joint crime case, where a defendant who has appealed dies and the other defendants have not appealed, the people's court of second instance shall still review the whole case. Upon review, if the deceased defendant is not guilty of a crime, an acquittal shall be pronounced; if guilty of a crime, the trial shall be terminated. Judgments or rulings shall still be rendered against the other co-defendants.

Article 313 In a criminal case with a collateral civil action, where only the parties to the collateral civil action or their legal representatives have appealed, the people's court of second instance shall review the whole case. Upon review, if the criminal part of the first instance judgment is not improper, the people's court of second instance shall only handle the collateral civil part; if the facts of the collateral civil part of the first instance judgment are clear and the law applied is correct, it shall uphold the original judgment and dismiss the appeal by a criminal-collateral civil ruling.

Article 314 In a criminal case with a collateral civil action, where only the parties to the collateral civil action or their legal representatives have appealed, the judgment on the criminal part of the first instance shall take legal effect upon the expiration of the appeal period.
Where a defendant in the first instance who is to be delivered for enforcement of imprisonment is also the defendant in the second instance collateral civil action, delivery for enforcement may be suspended pending the conclusion of the second instance collateral civil action.

Article 316 During the second instance, in addition to self-defense, the defendant may continue to retain the defender from the first instance or retain another defender to defend.
In a joint crime case, where only some of the defendants have appealed, or the private prosecutor has only appealed against the judgment concerning some of the defendants, or the People's Procuratorate has only protested against the judgment concerning some of the defendants, other co-defendants in the same case may also retain a defender to defend.

Article 318 With respect to cases of appeal or protest, if after review the people's court of second instance finds that the facts of the original judgment are unclear or the evidence is insufficient, or that there are circumstances violating statutory procedural rules as provided in Article 227 of the Criminal Procedure Law, and a remand for retrial is necessary, it may hear the case without holding a session in court.

Article 319 During the second instance, if the People's Procuratorate or the defendant or his defender submits new evidence, the people's court shall promptly notify the other party to inspect, extract or copy such evidence.

Article 320 Where a public prosecution case of second instance is tried in open court, the People's Procuratorate shall be promptly notified to review the case file after the decision to hold a session in court is made. From the day following the notification, the time spent by the People's Procuratorate in reviewing the case file shall not be counted in the trial period.

Article 321 Where a public prosecution case of appeal or protest is tried in open court, the People's Procuratorate at the same level shall be notified to send a procurator to appear in court. In a protest case, if the People's Procuratorate, after receiving the notice of court session, fails to send a procurator without stating the reason, the people's court may rule that the protest be deemed withdrawn, and shall notify the people's court of first instance and the parties.

Article 324 Where a second instance case is not tried in open court according to law, the defendant shall be interrogated and the opinions of other parties, defenders, and litigation agents shall be heard. All members of the collegial panel shall review the case file, and where necessary, shall submit written opinions on the file review.

Article 326 Where the People's Procuratorate only protests against the judgment concerning some of the defendants, or the private prosecutor only appeals against the judgment concerning some of the defendants, the people's court of second instance shall not aggravate the sentences of other co-defendants in the same case.

Article 327 In a case appealed by the defendant or his legal representative, defender, or close relative, after the people's court of second instance remands the case for retrial, the original trial court shall not aggravate the defendant's sentence, except where there are new criminal facts and the People's Procuratorate supplements the prosecution.

Article 328 In a case where the facts of the original judgment are unclear or the evidence is insufficient and the people's court of second instance remands the case for retrial, after the original trial court renders a new judgment, if the defendant appeals or the People's Procuratorate protests, the people's court of second instance shall render a judgment or ruling in accordance with law and shall not remand the case for retrial again.

Article 329 Where the people's court of second instance finds that the original trial court, during the retrial, had one of the circumstances provided in Article 227 of the Criminal Procedure Law, or violated the provisions of Article 228, it shall rule to set aside the original judgment and remand the case for retrial.

Article 330 Where the people's court of second instance, when adjudicating a case in which an appeal or protest is made against the criminal part and the collateral civil part has already taken legal effect, finds that the collateral civil part of the first instance judgment or ruling is indeed erroneous, it shall correct the collateral civil part in accordance with the trial supervision procedure.

Article 331 Where the people's court of second instance, when adjudicating a case in which an appeal is made against the collateral civil part and the criminal part has already taken legal effect, finds that the criminal part of the first instance judgment or ruling is indeed erroneous, it shall retry the criminal part in accordance with the trial supervision procedure and shall try the collateral civil part together with the criminal part.

Article 332 During the second instance, if the plaintiff in the collateral civil action in the first instance adds an independent claim or the defendant in the collateral civil action in the first instance files a counterclaim, the people's court of second instance may conduct mediation based on the principles of voluntariness and legality; if mediation fails, the parties shall be informed to file a separate lawsuit.

Article 333 For a private prosecution case in the second instance, mediation may be conducted where necessary, and the parties may also reach a settlement on their own. If the case is concluded by mediation, a mediation agreement shall be prepared, and the first instance judgment or ruling shall be deemed to have been automatically revoked; if the parties reach a settlement on their own, a ruling shall be made to permit the withdrawal of the private prosecution and to revoke the first instance judgment or ruling.
Article 334 During the second instance, if a party in a private prosecution case files a counterclaim, such party shall be informed to file a separate lawsuit.

Article 335 The people's court of second instance may entrust the people's court of first instance to pronounce the judgment on its behalf and to serve the second instance judgment or ruling on the parties. The people's court of first instance shall, within five days after pronouncing the judgment on behalf of the second instance court, deliver the record of pronouncement to the people's court of second instance, and promptly deliver the certificate of service to the people's court of second instance after service is completed.
Where the judgment is pronounced by entrustment, the people's court of second instance shall directly serve the second instance judgment or ruling on the People's Procuratorate at the same level.

Article 337 For a case submitted to the Supreme People's Court for approval of a sentence below the statutory punishment, five copies each of the judgment and the report requesting approval, as well as the complete case file and evidence, shall be submitted.

Article 338 For a case where a sentence below the statutory punishment has been imposed, if the Supreme People's Court approves, it shall issue a written ruling of approval; if it does not approve, it shall issue a written ruling of disapproval, set aside the original judgment or ruling, and remand the case to the original trial court for retrial or designate another lower people's court for retrial.

Article 339 Where a case is remanded to the people's court of second instance for retrial in accordance with Articles 336 and 338 of this Interpretation, the people's court of second instance may directly modify the judgment; if it is necessary to ascertain the facts, verify the evidence, or correct procedural violations in the original trial through a court session, the case shall be tried in open court.

Article 340 The trial period for the Supreme People's Court and higher people's courts to review cases involving sentences below the statutory punishment shall be governed by reference to the provisions of Article 232 of the Criminal Procedure Law.

Article 342 For a case submitted to the Supreme People's Court for approval of parole that is not limited by the executed term of sentence because the criminal has special circumstances, five copies each of the report requesting approval, the report on the criminal's special circumstances, and the parole ruling, as well as the complete case file, shall be submitted.

Article 343 For a case of parole that is not limited by the executed term of sentence because the criminal has special circumstances, if the Supreme People's Court approves, it shall issue a written ruling of approval; if it does not approve, it shall issue a written ruling of disapproval and revoke the original ruling.

Article 345 Where, in a first instance case in which the Intermediate People's Court imposes a death sentence with a two-year reprieve, the defendant has not appealed and the People's Procuratorate has not protested, the case shall be submitted to the Higher People's Court for approval.
The Higher People's Court, when reviewing a death sentence with a two-year reprieve case, shall interrogate the defendant.

Article 346 Cases of death sentence or death sentence with a two-year reprieve submitted for review shall be reported on a case-by-case basis. The materials submitted shall include the report requesting review, five copies each of the first and second instance adjudicative documents and the comprehensive report on the death sentence case, as well as the complete case file and evidence. The comprehensive report on the death sentence case, the first and second instance adjudicative documents, and the trial report shall be accompanied by electronic copies.
Cases tried jointly shall be submitted with the complete case file and evidence.
For cases that were previously remanded for retrial, the original first and second instance case files shall be submitted together.

Article 351: For a case of combined punishment for multiple crimes where a person is sentenced to death for two or more crimes, if after review the Supreme People's Court considers that the death sentence or ruling for some of the crimes has unclear facts or insufficient evidence, it shall rule not to approve the entire case, revoke the original judgment, and remand for retrial; if it considers that the death sentence or ruling for some of the crimes correctly determines the facts but the death penalty should not have been imposed according to law, it may alter the sentence and render a judgment approving the death penalty for the other crimes for which the death penalty should be imposed.

Article 352: For a case where two or more defendants are sentenced to death, if after review the Supreme People's Court considers that the death sentence or ruling for some defendants has unclear facts or insufficient evidence, it shall rule not to approve the entire case, revoke the original judgment, and remand for retrial; if it considers that the death sentence or ruling for some defendants correctly determines the facts but the death penalty should not have been imposed according to law, it may alter the sentence and render a judgment approving the death penalty for the other defendants who should be sentenced to death.

Article 353: If the Supreme People's Court rules not to approve a death sentence, it may, according to the circumstances of the case, remand the case to the Second Instance People's Court or the First Instance People's Court for retrial.
If the First Instance People's Court conducts a retrial, it shall hold a court session for trial. If the Second Instance People's Court conducts a retrial, it may directly alter the sentence; if it is necessary to clarify the facts, verify the evidence, or correct procedural violations of the original trial through a court session, it shall hold a court session for trial.

Article 354: If a Higher People's Court, after trial in accordance with the review procedure, reports to the Supreme People's Court for approval of a death sentence, and the Supreme People's Court rules not to approve and remands the case to the Higher People's Court for retrial, the Higher People's Court may either bring the case up for trial in accordance with the second instance procedure or remand it for retrial.

Article 355: For a case where the Supreme People's Court rules not to approve the death penalty and remands for retrial, the original trial people's court shall form a new collegial panel to hear the case, except for the cases specified in items (4) and (5) of Article 350 of this Interpretation.

Article 356: During the period of death penalty review, if the defense lawyer requests to present opinions in person, the relevant collegial panel of the Supreme People's Court shall hear the lawyer's opinions in the office and make a record; if the defense lawyer submits written opinions, they shall be attached to the case file.

Article 357: During the period of death penalty review, if the Supreme People's Procuratorate presents opinions, the Supreme People's Court shall review them and provide feedback to the Supreme People's Procuratorate on the status of adoption and the reasons therefor.
Article 358: The Supreme People's Court shall, in accordance with relevant provisions, notify the Supreme People's Procuratorate of the results of the review of death penalty cases.

Article 359: A people's court shall properly keep the defendant's property and its fruits that have been sealed up, seized, or frozen, and shall make a list thereof to be attached to the case file for future reference; for the defendant's property and its fruits transferred by the People's Procuratorate with the case, it shall verify them against the list and then keep them properly. No unit or individual may misappropriate or dispose of them without authorization.
When sealing up immovable property, vehicles, ships, aircraft, or other property, the court shall seize the title certificates, seal them up on the spot after taking photographs or making a video recording, or deliver them to the holder or a close relative of the defendant for custody, register and record detailed information such as the name, model, ownership, and address of the property, and notify the relevant registration and administrative authorities of the property to go through the formalities for registration of the seal-up.
When seizing items, the court shall register and record the name, model, specifications, quantity, weight, quality, fineness, purity, color, degree of newness, defect characteristics, and source of the items, etc. When seizing currency or negotiable securities, the court shall register and record the name, amount, denomination, etc. of the currency or negotiable securities; currency shall be deposited into a special bank account, and the name and content of the bank deposit certificate shall be recorded. When seizing cultural relics, gold, silver, jewelry, valuable calligraphy and paintings, or other valuable items and contraband, the court shall take photographs; if appraisal is necessary, it shall promptly conduct the appraisal. The seized items shall be promptly valued in accordance with relevant provisions.
When freezing property such as deposits, remittances, bonds, stocks, or fund shares, the court shall register and record the serial number, type, face value, number of certificates, amount, etc.

Article 360: For the lawful property of a victim, if the ownership is clear, it shall be promptly returned according to law, provided that photographs, appraisal, and valuation are undertaken, and the reasons for the return shall be noted in the case file, with photographs of the original items, a list, and the victim's receipt documents attached to the file for future reference; if the ownership is unclear, the property shall be returned to the victim in proportion after the people's court's judgment or ruling takes effect, provided that the portion already compensated shall be deducted.

Article 361: During the trial period, if the right holder applies to sell the seized or frozen property such as bonds, stocks, or fund shares, and the people's court, after examination, considers that it does not harm the interests of the state or the victim and does not affect the normal progress of the litigation, or if the validity period of the seized or frozen bills of exchange, promissory notes, or checks is about to expire, the court may sell such property according to law before the judgment or ruling takes effect; the proceeds therefrom shall be kept by the people's court, and the parties or their close relatives shall be promptly notified.

Article 362: Tangible objects used as evidence, including currency, negotiable securities, etc., used as physical evidence, shall be transferred with the case. After the first instance judgment or ruling is pronounced, if the defendant appeals or the People's Procuratorate protests, the First Instance People's Court shall transfer the aforesaid evidence to the Second Instance People's Court.

Article 364: During the court trial, the ownership status of the property and its fruits that have been sealed up, seized, or frozen shall be investigated, specifically whether they constitute illegal gains or other property involved in the case that should be recovered according to law.
If a person not involved in the case raises an objection to the ownership of the sealed-up, seized, or frozen property and its fruits, the people's court shall examine and handle it according to law.
If, after examination, it cannot be confirmed that the sealed-up, seized, or frozen property and its fruits are illegal gains or other property involved in the case that should be recovered according to law, they shall not be confiscated.

Article 365: For the property and its fruits that have been sealed up, seized, or frozen, the judgment shall specify the name, amount, quantity, storage location, and method of disposition, etc. If there is a large amount of property involved in the case, and it is not appropriate to list them in detail in the main text of the judgment, a list may be attached.
If the property involved in the case is not transferred with the case, the judgment shall specify that fact and state that the authority that sealed up, seized, or frozen the property shall be responsible for handling it.

Article 366: If, after examination, the sealed-up, seized, or frozen property and its fruits are confirmed to be illegal gains or other property involved in the case that should be recovered according to law, the judgment shall order their return to the victim or their confiscation and surrender to the State Treasury, unless otherwise provided by law.
For the property involved in the case that is adjudged to be returned to the victim, the victim shall be notified to claim it; if no one claims it, a public notice shall be issued; if no one claims it within three months after the public notice, the property shall be surrendered to the State Treasury; if after surrender to the State Treasury someone claims it and the claim is verified, an application shall be made for withdrawal from the Treasury to return it; if the original items have been auctioned or sold, the proceeds shall be returned.
For cases involving infringement of State property, if the victim unit has been terminated and has no successor of rights and obligations, or if the losses have been written off, the sealed-up, seized, or frozen property and its fruits shall be surrendered to the State Treasury.

Article 367: The property and its fruits that are transferred with the case or sealed up or seized by the people's court shall be handled by the First Instance People's Court after the judgment takes effect.
If the property involved in the case is not transferred with the case, the people's court shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, serve the judgment or ruling on the authority that sealed up or seized the property, and inform it to return the execution receipt within one month.

Article 368: If a judgment orders the confiscation of frozen property such as deposits, remittances, bonds, stocks, or fund shares, the First Instance People's Court shall, after the judgment takes effect, serve the judgment or ruling on the relevant financial institution and the financial department, notify the relevant financial institution to surrender the property to the State Treasury according to law, and within fifteen days after receiving the enforcement notice, return the certificate of surrender to the State Treasury and the execution receipt.

Article 369: If the sealed-up, seized, or frozen property is not related to the case but has been included in the list, it shall be handled by the authority that sealed up, seized, or frozen it according to law.
If the sealed-up, seized, or frozen property belongs to the defendant lawfully, it shall be timely returned to the defendant after compensating the victim for losses and executing the property penalty; if the property is not transferred with the case, the authority that sealed up, seized, or frozen it shall be notified to transfer to the people's court the portion used to compensate the victim for losses and execute the property penalty.

Article 370: For matters concerning the sealing up, seizure, freezing, and disposition of property that are not provided for in this Interpretation, the relevant provisions of laws and other judicial interpretations shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 371: If a party, his legal representative, or a close relative files a petition against a legally effective judgment or ruling, the people's court shall examine and handle it.
If a person not involved in the case files a petition on the grounds that a legally effective judgment or ruling infringes upon his lawful rights and interests, the people's court shall examine and handle it.
A petition may be filed through a lawyer by mandate.

Article 373: A petition shall be examined and handled by the final-instance people's court. However, for a case where the second-instance people's court has ruled to permit the withdrawal of an appeal, if the petitioner files a petition against the first-instance judgment, the first-instance people's court may examine and handle it.
If a petition has not been examined by the final-instance people's court, the people's court at the next higher level may inform the petitioner to file the petition with the final-instance people's court, or directly refer the petition to the final-instance people's court for examination and handling, and inform the petitioner accordingly; if the case is difficult, complex, or significant, it may also directly examine and handle it.
If a petition is filed directly with a higher-level people's court without being examined by the final-instance people's court or its next higher-level court, the higher-level people's court may inform the petitioner to file the petition with the lower-level people's court.

Article 374: For a petition against a death penalty case, the people's court that originally approved the death penalty may directly examine and handle it, or may refer it to the original trial people's court for examination. The original trial people's court shall prepare an examination report, put forward handling opinions, and report them level by level to the people's court that originally approved the death penalty for examination and handling.

Article 377: If a petitioner refuses to accept the rejection of the petition, he may file a petition with the people's court at the next higher level. If the people's court at the next higher level, after examination, considers that the petition does not comply with the provisions of Article 242 of the Criminal Procedure Law and paragraph 2 of Article 375 of this Interpretation, it shall persuade the petitioner to withdraw the petition; if the petitioner still insists on the petition, it shall reject the petition or notify that no retrial shall be conducted.

Article 378: If the president of a people's court at any level discovers that a legally effective judgment or ruling of that court is indeed erroneous, he shall submit it to the judicial committee for discussion to decide whether to initiate a retrial.

Article 379: If a higher-level people's court discovers that a legally effective judgment or ruling of a lower-level people's court is indeed erroneous, it may direct the lower-level people's court to conduct a retrial; if the facts determined by the original judgment or ruling are correct but the law is incorrectly applied, or if the case is difficult, complex, or significant, or if there are circumstances that make it inappropriate for the original trial people's court to hear the case, the higher-level people's court may also bring the case up for trial itself.
If a higher-level people's court directs a lower-level people's court to conduct a retrial, it shall generally direct a lower-level people's court other than the original trial people's court to hear the case; if trial by the original trial people's court is more conducive to clarifying the facts of the case and correcting errors in the judgment, it may direct the original trial people's court to hear the case.

Article 381: For a case in which the People's Procuratorate files a protest in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the people's court that accepts the protest shall form a collegial panel to hear the case. If the facts of the original judgment are unclear or the evidence is insufficient, including where new evidence proves that the original judgment may be erroneous, and it is necessary to direct a lower-level people's court to conduct a retrial, a decision shall be made within one month from the date of case filing, and the decision on directing a retrial shall be served on the protesting People's Procuratorate.

Article 382: For a case that has been decided to be retried in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, except for cases protested by the People's Procuratorate, the people's court shall issue a retrial decision. During the retrial, the enforcement of the original judgment or ruling shall not be suspended; however, if the defendant may be acquitted upon retrial, or if the original punishment may be reduced upon retrial resulting in the expiration of the term of sentence, the court may decide to suspend the enforcement of the original judgment or ruling, and if necessary, may adopt measures of release on bail pending investigation or trial or residential surveillance against the defendant.

Article 383: For a case retried in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the people's court shall focus the trial on the grounds of the petition, the protest, and the decision to retry. When necessary, a comprehensive review shall be conducted on the facts, evidence, and application of law determined in the original judgment or ruling.

Article 384: When the original trial people's court hears a case retried in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, it shall form a new collegial panel.
If the case was originally a first-instance case, it shall be tried in accordance with the first-instance procedure, and the judgment or ruling rendered may be appealed or protested; if the case was originally a second-instance case, or a case brought up for trial by a higher-level people's court, it shall be tried in accordance with the second-instance procedure, and the judgment or ruling rendered shall be a final judgment or ruling.
For a retrial case where the original defendant or the original private prosecutor has died or lost capacity for conduct, the court may not hold a court session for trial.

Article 385: For a retrial case tried with a court session, if the retrial decision or protest letter only targets some of the original defendants, and the absence of other co-defendants in the original case does not affect the trial, those other defendants may not appear in court to participate in the proceedings.

Article 386: Except for cases protested by the People's Procuratorate, the punishment of the original defendant shall generally not be increased upon retrial. If the retrial decision or protest letter only targets some of the original defendants, the punishment of other co-defendants in the original case shall not be increased.

Article 387: When a people's court hears a retrial case protested by the People's Procuratorate, if the People's Procuratorate withdraws the protest before the court session, the court shall rule to permit the withdrawal; if the People's Procuratorate, after receiving the notice to appear in court, fails to send a representative to appear without stating reasons, the court may rule to treat the protest as withdrawn and notify the participants in the proceedings.
When a people's court hears a retrial case initiated by a petitioner's petition, if the petitioner withdraws the petition during the retrial period, the court shall rule to permit the withdrawal; if the petitioner, after being notified according to law, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, or leaves the courtroom without the permission of the court during the trial, the court shall rule to treat the petition as withdrawn, except where the petitioner is not the original party.

Article 388 In a retrial case heard in open court, if the retrial is decided by the People's Court, the members of the collegial panel shall read the retrial decision; if the case is protested by the People's Procuratorate, the procuratorial personnel shall read the protest letter; if the case is upon the petition of the petitioner, the petitioner or his or her defender or litigation agent shall state the grounds for the petition.

Article 390 If the original judgment or ruling has errors in identifying the defendant's name or other identity information but is correct in finding facts and applying law and the sentence is appropriate, the People's Court that rendered the effective judgment or ruling may correct the relevant information by a ruling.

Article 391 For a party who is acquitted upon retrial and is entitled to apply for state compensation according to law, the People's Court, when pronouncing judgment, shall inform the party that he or she may apply for state compensation according to law after the judgment takes effect.

Article 393 Foreign-related criminal cases of first instance shall be under the jurisdiction of the Primary People's Court, except those specified in Articles 20 to 22 of the Criminal Procedure Law. Where necessary, the Intermediate People's Court may designate several Primary People's Courts within its jurisdiction to centrally exercise jurisdiction over foreign-related criminal cases of first instance, or may try foreign-related criminal cases of first instance that fall under the jurisdiction of the Primary People's Court in accordance with the provisions of Article 23 of the Criminal Procedure Law.

Article 394 The nationality of a foreigner shall be determined based on the valid documents at the time of entry; if the nationality is unclear, it shall be determined based on the certificate issued by the public security organ or the embassy or consulate of the relevant country in China.
If the nationality cannot be ascertained, the person shall be treated as a stateless person, the relevant provisions of this Chapter shall apply, and "nationality unknown" shall be stated in the judgment documents.
Article 395 In criminal proceedings, foreign parties shall enjoy the litigation rights provided for by the laws of China and bear corresponding obligations.

Article 396 During the trial of a foreign-related criminal case, the People's Court shall promptly notify the foreign affairs department of the people's government at the same level and inform the embassy or consulate of the relevant country in China of the following matters:
(1) The situation where the People's Court decides to take compulsory measures against a foreign defendant, including the name (including transliteration), gender, time of entry, passport or document number, the compulsory measures taken and the legal basis, the place of custody, etc.;
(2) The time and place of the court session, whether the trial is open to the public, and other matters;
(3) The time and place of the pronouncement of judgment.
After the judgment of a foreign-related criminal case is pronounced, the result shall be promptly reported to the foreign affairs department of the people's government at the same level.
If the death penalty is to be executed on a foreign defendant, the embassy or consulate of his or her country of nationality in China shall be notified after the death penalty decision is issued and before the execution.
If a foreign defendant dies during the trial, the matter shall be promptly reported to the foreign affairs department of the people's government at the same level and the embassy or consulate of the relevant country in China shall be informed.

Article 398 After accepting a foreign-related criminal case, the People's Court shall inform the foreign defendant in custody that he or she has the right to contact the embassy or consulate of his or her country of nationality in China, to meet and correspond with his or her guardians and close relatives, and to request the People's Court to provide interpretation services.

Article 399 During the trial of a foreign-related criminal case, if a foreign defendant is in custody and an official of the embassy or consulate of his or her country of nationality in China requests to visit, the request may be submitted to the Higher People's Court in the locality of the People's Court trying the case. The People's Court shall arrange the visit within the time limit prescribed by the bilateral consular treaty concluded between China and the defendant's country of nationality; if no such treaty exists, arrangements shall be made as soon as possible. Where necessary, the assistance of the foreign affairs department of the people's government may be sought.
During the trial of a foreign-related criminal case, if a foreign defendant is in custody and his or her guardians or close relatives apply for a meeting, the application may be submitted to the Higher People's Court in the locality of the People's Court trying the case, and evidence of the relationship with the defendant shall be provided in accordance with Article 403 of this Interpretation. The People's Court, after examination, may approve the meeting if it finds that it does not hinder the trial of the case.
If the defendant refuses to receive a visit or meeting, the arrangement may be omitted, but the defendant shall provide a written statement to that effect.
Visits and meetings with the defendant shall comply with the laws and regulations of China.

Article 400 The People's Court shall try foreign-related criminal cases in open court, except for those that shall not be tried in public according to law.
In a foreign-related criminal case tried in open court, if an official of the embassy or consulate of the country of nationality of a foreign party requests to observe the trial, the request may be submitted to the Higher People's Court in the locality of the People's Court trying the case, and the People's Court shall make arrangements.

Article 401 When trying a foreign-related criminal case, the People's Court shall use the commonly used language and characters of the People's Republic of China and shall provide interpretation for foreign parties.
The litigation documents of the People's Court shall be in Chinese. If a foreign party does not understand Chinese, a translation in a foreign language shall be attached. The translation shall not be affixed with the seal of the People's Court, and the Chinese version shall prevail.
If a foreign party understands the Chinese language and characters, refuses any interpretation, or does not need a foreign language translation of the litigation documents, he or she shall provide a written statement to that effect.

Article 402 If a foreign defendant entrusts a lawyer to defend, or a foreign plaintiff in an incidental civil action or a foreign private prosecutor entrusts a lawyer to act as agent ad litem, the lawyer shall be one who possesses the qualification of a lawyer of the People's Republic of China and has obtained a practicing certificate according to law.
If a foreign defendant is in custody, his or her guardians, close relatives, or the embassy or consulate of his or her country of nationality in China may entrust a defender on his or her behalf. If the guardians or close relatives entrust a defender on his or her behalf, they shall provide valid evidence of their relationship with the defendant.
If a foreign party entrusts his or her guardians or close relatives to act as defender or litigation agent, the entrusted person shall provide valid evidence of the relationship with the party. After examination, if the requirements of the Criminal Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations are met, the People's Court shall permit such appointment.
If a foreign defendant does not have a defender, the People's Court may notify a legal aid institution to assign a lawyer to provide defense. If the defendant refuses the defense of a defender, he or she shall provide a written statement to that effect, or his or her oral statement shall be recorded. If the defendant falls under the circumstances where legal aid shall be provided, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 45 of this Interpretation.

Article 403 A power of attorney sent or entrusted by a foreign party from outside the territory of the People's Republic of China to a Chinese lawyer or Chinese citizen, and the evidence of relationship provided by the guardians or close relatives of a foreign party, shall be notarized by a notary office of the country where they are located, authenticated by the central foreign affairs authority or its authorized organ of that country, and authenticated by the embassy or consulate of China in that country, unless an agreement on mutual exemption of authentication exists between China and that country.

Article 404 For a defendant in a foreign-related criminal case, a decision may be made to restrict his or her departure from China; for a witness who must be present at the court session, a request may be made to temporarily postpone his or her departure. A decision to restrict departure shall be reported to the public security organ or state security organ at the same level; if the person whose departure is restricted is a foreigner, it shall also be reported to the foreign affairs department of the people's government at the same level and the embassy or consulate of the party's country of nationality in China.
If the People's Court decides to restrict the departure of a foreigner or a Chinese citizen, it shall notify the restricted person in writing that he or she shall not leave China before the conclusion of the trial, and may take the measure of detaining the passport or other exit-entry documents to restrict departure; if documents are detained, necessary formalities shall be completed, and a certificate of detention shall be issued to the person.
If it is necessary to prevent a foreigner or a Chinese citizen from leaving China at a border inspection station, the People's Court trying the case shall report level by level to the Higher People's Court, which shall fill out a Notice on Preventing the Departure of a Person at the Port and go through the control procedures with the public security organ at the same level. If the port of control is not within the same province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, the control procedures shall be handled through the public security organ of the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government. In an emergency, if truly necessary, the control may be handed over to the border inspection station first, and the control procedures may be completed afterwards.

Article 405 For evidentiary materials originating from outside the territory of China, the People's Court shall examine the source of the materials, the provider, the time of provision, the person who obtained them, and the time of obtaining, among other things. After examination, if such materials can prove the facts of the case and comply with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, they may be used as evidence, except where the provider or a bilateral treaty concluded between China and the relevant country imposes explicit restrictions on the scope of use; if the source of the materials is unknown or their authenticity cannot be confirmed, they shall not be used as the basis for deciding the case.
If a party, his or her defender, or litigation agent provides evidentiary materials from outside the territory of China, such materials shall be notarized by a notary office of the country where they are located, authenticated by the central foreign affairs authority or its authorized organ of that country, and authenticated by the embassy or consulate of China in that country.

Article 406 For a foreign-related criminal case that meets the requirements of Article 202, paragraph 1, and Article 232 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the trial period may be extended upon approval or decision of the relevant People's Court.

Article 407 After the judgment of a foreign-related criminal case is pronounced, if the embassy or consulate of the country of nationality of a foreign party requests to be provided with the judgment document, the request may be submitted to the Higher People's Court in the locality of the People's Court trying the case, and the People's Court may provide it.

Article 408 In accordance with international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China, or on the basis of the principle of reciprocity, the People's Court and foreign courts may request criminal judicial assistance from each other.
If the matter requested by a foreign court is detrimental to the sovereignty, security, or public interests of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall not provide assistance.

Article 409 Requests for and provision of judicial assistance shall be made through the channels prescribed by the international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China; if no treaty relationship exists, it shall be done through diplomatic channels.

Article 410 If a People's Court requests a foreign country to provide judicial assistance, it shall be reviewed by the Higher People's Court and then reported to the Supreme People's Court for examination and approval.
If a foreign court requests China to provide judicial assistance and the matter falls within the functions and powers of the People's Court, it shall be transmitted to the relevant People's Court for handling after examination and approval by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 411 A letter of request submitted by the People's Court to a foreign country for judicial assistance and the attached documents shall be accompanied by a translation in the language of that country or a text in another language as prescribed by an international treaty.
A letter of request submitted by a foreign court to China for judicial assistance and the attached documents shall be accompanied by a Chinese translation or a text in another language as prescribed by an international treaty.

Article 413 If the People's Court serves criminal litigation documents through diplomatic channels on a recipient residing outside the territory of the People's Republic of China, the documents to be served shall be reviewed by the Higher People's Court and then reported to the Supreme People's Court for examination. If the Supreme People's Court considers that the documents may be sent, it shall hand them over to the competent department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for transmission.
If a foreign court requests the People's Court to serve criminal litigation documents through diplomatic channels, the embassy of that country in China shall hand over the legal documents to the competent department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China for transmission to the Supreme People's Court. After examination, if the Supreme People's Court considers that the matter falls within the functions and powers of the People's Court and can be served on behalf, it shall transmit the documents to the relevant People's Court for handling.
Article 414 Other matters arising during the trial of a foreign-related criminal case shall be handled in accordance with laws, judicial interpretations, and other relevant provisions.

Article 415 If a criminal who is sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve commits an intentional crime during the period of reprieve, the case shall be tried by the Intermediate People's Court in the place where the criminal is serving the sentence according to law, and the judgment rendered may be appealed or protested.
After the judgment or ruling finding the intentional crime is established and becomes legally effective, it shall be reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court for approval of execution of the death penalty.

Article 416 The period of a death sentence with a two-year reprieve shall be calculated from the date on which the legal document approving the death sentence with a two-year reprieve is pronounced or served.
Upon the expiration of the period of the death sentence with a two-year reprieve, if the penalty shall be commuted according to law, the People's Court shall promptly commute the sentence. If the death sentence with a two-year reprieve is commuted to life imprisonment or fixed-term imprisonment upon expiration, the term of imprisonment shall be calculated from the date on which the period of the reprieve expires.

Article 417 The execution order for the death penalty issued by the Supreme People's Court shall be transmitted by the Higher People's Court to the People's Court of first instance for execution. Upon receiving the execution order, the People's Court of first instance shall execute it within seven days.
If an intentional crime is committed during the period of a death sentence with a two-year reprieve and the Supreme People's Court approves the execution of the death penalty, the execution shall be carried out by the Intermediate People's Court in the place where the criminal is serving the sentence.

Article 419 If, after the execution order for the death penalty is issued but before execution, the Supreme People's Court discovers any of the circumstances specified in paragraph 1 of the preceding article, it shall immediately rule to suspend the execution of the death penalty and transfer the relevant materials to the lower People's Court.

Article 420 After receiving the Supreme People's Court's ruling to suspend the execution of the death penalty, the lower People's Court shall, together with relevant departments, investigate and verify the reasons for the suspension, and promptly report the investigation results and opinions level by level to the Supreme People's Court for review.

Article 421 The investigation results and opinions submitted by the lower People's Court regarding the suspension of execution of the death penalty shall be reviewed by the collegial panel of the Supreme People's Court that originally rendered the judgment or ruling approving the death penalty. If necessary, a separate collegial panel shall be formed for review.

Article 423 Before executing the death penalty, the People's Court of first instance shall inform the criminal of the right to meet with his or her close relatives. If the criminal applies for a meeting and provides specific contact information, the People's Court shall notify his or her close relatives. If the close relatives of the criminal apply for a meeting, the People's Court shall permit it and promptly arrange the meeting.

Article 424 The Primary People's Court that tried the case shall, three days before the execution of the death penalty, notify the People's Procuratorate at the same level to designate an officer to supervise the execution on site.

Article 425 The death penalty shall be executed by means of shooting, injection, or other methods.
Where the death penalty is executed by injection, it shall be executed at a designated execution ground or within a detention facility.
Where the death penalty is executed by methods other than shooting or injection, prior approval from the Supreme People's Court shall be obtained through report by levels.

Article 426 Before the execution of the death penalty, the judicial officer directing the execution shall verify the identity of the criminal, ask whether he or she has any dying words or letters, and make a record thereof, and then deliver the criminal to the executing officers for execution of the death penalty.
The execution of the death penalty shall be announced, and parading the criminal in public or any other act that humiliates the personality of the criminal is prohibited.

Article 427 After the execution of the death penalty, a forensic medical examiner shall verify that the criminal is indeed dead, and the court clerk present shall make a record. The People's Court responsible for the execution shall, within fifteen days after the execution of the death penalty, report the execution circumstances, including photos of the criminal before and after the execution of the death penalty, to the Supreme People's Court.

Article 429 Where a criminal sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, life imprisonment, fixed-term imprisonment, or criminal detention is in custody when handed over for execution, the Primary People's Court shall, within ten days after the judgment or ruling takes effect, deliver the judgment, ruling, copy of the bill of prosecution, copy of the private prosecution complaint, execution notice, and case closure registration form to the detention center, and the public security organ shall hand over the criminal for execution.
Where a criminal needs to be taken into custody to serve the sentence but was not held in custody before the judgment or ruling took effect, the People's Court shall, based on the effective judgment or ruling, deliver the criminal to the detention center for custody, and handle the execution procedures in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 430 In a case tried jointly, where some defendants are sentenced to death and other co-defendants who are not sentenced to death need to be held in custody to serve their sentences, execution shall be carried out within ten days after their judgments or rulings take effect. However, if such a co-defendant participated in the commission of the crime for which the death penalty is imposed, execution shall be carried out after the Supreme People's Court has reviewed and interrogated the defendant sentenced to death.
Article 431 The receipt of the execution notice, after being stamped by the detention center, shall be attached to the case file for reference.

Article 432 Where a criminal sentenced to life imprisonment, fixed-term imprisonment, or criminal detention meets the conditions specified in paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 254 of the Criminal Procedure Law, and the People's Court decides to grant temporary service of sentence outside prison, it shall issue a decision on temporary service of sentence outside prison, specifying the basic information of the criminal, the crime and penalty determined by the judgment, the reasons and legal basis for the decision on temporary service of sentence outside prison, etc., notify the judicial administrative organ at the county level where the criminal resides to send personnel to handle the transfer procedures, and serve a copy of the decision on temporary service of sentence outside prison to the People's Procuratorate and the public security organ at the county level where the criminal resides.
Where the People's Procuratorate considers the People's Court's decision on temporary service of sentence outside prison to be improper and submits a written opinion within the statutory time limit, the People's Court shall immediately re-examine the decision and make a decision within one month.

Article 434 The People's Court shall deliver the decision on execution in prison to the judicial administrative organ at the county level where the criminal resides, which shall hand over the criminal for execution in accordance with relevant provisions. The decision on execution in prison shall also be served simultaneously to the People's Procuratorate and the public security organ at the same level where the criminal resides.

Article 435 Where a criminal subject to execution in prison has circumstances that shall not be counted into the term of imprisonment served, the People's Court shall, at the time of making the decision on execution in prison, determine the specific period that shall not be counted into the term of imprisonment served.

Article 436 For a criminal sentenced to public surveillance or placed on probation, the People's Court shall verify his or her place of residence. At the time of pronouncement of judgment, the court shall inform the criminal in writing of the time limit for reporting to the judicial administrative organ at the county level of his or her place of residence and the consequences of failing to report on time. Within ten days after the judgment or ruling takes effect, the court shall serve the judgment, ruling, execution notice, and other legal documents to the judicial administrative organ at the county level where the criminal resides, and at the same time serve a copy to the People's Procuratorate at the county level where the criminal resides.

Article 437 For a criminal sentenced solely to deprivation of political rights, the People's Court shall, within ten days after the judgment or ruling takes effect, serve the judgment, ruling, execution notice, and other legal documents to the public security organ at the county level where the criminal resides, and serve a copy to the People's Procuratorate at the county level where the criminal resides.
Article 438 The execution of pecuniary penalties and incidental civil judgments shall be carried out by the organ responsible for the execution of judgments and rulings of the Primary People's Court.

Article 439 A fine shall be paid in a lump sum or in installments within the period specified in the judgment. If the fine is not paid or is not paid in full without just cause upon expiration of the period, the People's Court shall enforce payment. If the fine still cannot be fully paid after enforcement, at any time, including after the principal punishment has been executed, if property of the person subject to enforcement is found to be available for execution, the amount shall be recovered.
Where an administrative authority has already imposed a fine on the defendant for the same facts, when the People's Court imposes a fine, it shall offset the amount and deduct the portion already executed as an administrative penalty.
Where confiscation of property is imposed, execution shall be carried out immediately after the judgment takes effect.

Article 440 In the process of executing pecuniary penalties and incidental civil judgments, if a person not involved in the case raises an objection to the ownership of the property subject to execution, the People's Court shall review and handle the matter by reference to the provisions on execution objections in civil litigation.

Article 441 Where a person subject to enforcement is sentenced to a pecuniary penalty and at the same time bears incidental civil compensation liability, he or she shall first perform the civil compensation liability.
Where a person subject to enforcement owes legitimate debts before the imposition of the pecuniary penalty that need to be repaid with the property subject to execution, such debts shall be repaid upon the request of the creditor.

Article 442 Where the person subject to enforcement or the property subject to execution is located in another place, execution may be entrusted to the local People's Court.
After executing a pecuniary penalty, the entrusted court shall promptly turn over the executed property to the state treasury.

Article 445 Where a pecuniary penalty is wholly or partially revoked, the property already executed shall be wholly or partially returned to the person subject to enforcement; if return is impossible, compensation shall be made in accordance with law.

Article 446 Where a person subject to enforcement applies for reduction or exemption of a fine due to genuine difficulty in paying the fine caused by irresistible disaster, he or she shall submit relevant supporting materials.
